scout.purpose: Kotlin Android programs execute on ART using JVM-oriented bytecode and regularly cross Java APIs, so source-level convenience must be connected to runtime representation.
scout.realWorldUse: Platform APIs and many libraries expose Java signatures; performance diagnosis requires recognising boxing, object reachability, allocation, and platform nullability.
scout.outcome: Handle Java platform types defensively and reason about references, equality, boxing, allocation, and garbage-collection reachability.

sections.title: Java boundaries weaken some Kotlin guarantees

blocks.text: Java declarations without recognised nullability metadata appear as platform types, displayed informally as T!. Kotlin lets the caller treat a platform value as nullable or non-null, so an incorrect assumption can still cause a runtime null failure. Convert platform data at the boundary into an explicit Kotlin type, validate it, and avoid letting uncertain platform types spread. Java void maps to Unit, checked exceptions are not enforced by Kotlin, and mapped collection types require attention to mutability.

blocks.caption: An explicit nullable type restores visible null handling at the Java boundary.

blocks.title: Interop boundary
rows: Int with runtime primitive representation when possible
May propagate without a required catch declaration

sections.title: Variables hold values or references according to representation

blocks.text: Objects are reached through references; assigning one ordinary object variable to another usually makes both names refer to the same instance. Structural equality with == calls equals, while referential equality with === asks whether references identify the same object. Data classes provide value-based structural equality. Mutation through one alias is visible through another, which is why immutable values and defensive collection boundaries reduce surprising shared state.

blocks.code:
data class Draft(val category: String)
val first = Draft("Food")
val second = first.copy()
println(first == second)  // equal values
println(first === second) // different instances
blocks.caption: Structural and referential equality answer different questions even when data matches.

blocks.title: Reachability, not scope alone
blocks.text: Garbage collection can reclaim an object after no live root can reach it; leaving a lexical block is not the complete rule.

sections.title: Source syntax does not guarantee runtime shape

blocks.text: Kotlin number values often use JVM primitive representations, but generics and nullable primitives may require boxed objects. Lambdas that capture variables can allocate function objects unless inlining removes them. Collection transformations may allocate intermediate collections, and object creation inside frequently repeated UI or data work can create garbage-collection pressure. This does not justify premature micro-optimisation. First choose clear types, then use profilers and benchmarks to locate allocations that affect latency, memory, or battery.

blocks.code:
val direct: Int = 7             // often primitive
val nullable: Int? = 7          // may require boxing
val generic: List<Int> = listOf(7) // elements use boxed representation

val factor = 2
val scale: (Int) -> Int = { it * factor } // captures factor
blocks.caption: Equivalent-looking source values may require different runtime representations at generic, nullable, or captured boundaries.

inspect.title: Compare equality and aliasing
inspect.code:
data class Expense(var amount: Double)
fun main() {
    val original = Expense(5.0)
    val alias = original
    val copy = original.copy()
    alias.amount = 9.0
    println(original.amount)
    println(original === alias)
    println(original === copy)
}
walkthrough: alias and original refer to the same mutable object.
Changing through alias is visible through original.
copy begins with equal data but is a different instance.

trap_check.mistake: Trusting an unannotated Java String as definitely non-null.
trap_check.why: A platform type may contain null despite convenient Kotlin syntax.
trap_check.fix: Assign an explicit nullable type and validate at the boundary.

trap_check.why: The change may add complexity without affecting the real bottleneck.
trap_check.fix: Profile representative work, change one cause, and measure again.

challenge_intro.task: Write a Kotlin adapter around a hypothetical Java expense record with platform strings and boxed numbers, producing a validated immutable Kotlin model.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Platform values do not escape the adapter. Nullability and conversion failures become explicit outcomes. No non-null assertion is used for uncertain Java data.

recall.answer: A Java-origin type whose nullability Kotlin cannot determine safely.
== checks structural equality and === checks reference identity.
